start_here: Say to your AI: "Decide which Instagram messages from account-one my reply rules answer now." It runs tool:decide-the-replies with place reply-place:instagram and tells you each reply to send, and which it leaves and why. It sends nothing.

lists.label: Reply rules
lists.holds: One keyword rule: the words that pick it, whether any or all must match, the reply it sends and where it comes in the order.

values.reply: Hi, the price list is here: https://example.com/prices
We are open 9 to 5, Monday to Friday.

alike: saved replies in a help desk
keyword auto-replies in a social inbox tool

instructions: 1. Pour the two example reply rules into your own saved-replies list (see pour), or make list:reply-rules from them. A rule is used only when On or off is on; the first on rule in Order whose words match decides the reply.

2. Pull the place first (an Instagram account's messages and comments are pulled and kept under a name such as account-one) or, for YouTube, run tool:read-youtube-comments and hand its answers in as pulled.comment.

3. Say "Decide my replies for Instagram": the AI runs tool:decide-the-replies at @workshop-tools with {place: "reply-place:instagram", account: "<the name the pulls were kept under>"}; add account_id for a place that reads your own id from your connection (YouTube).
4. Read decisions: each has action send (with reply_text, key, kind and recipient) or skip (with a reason such as already-sent or comment-is-ours), and not_pulled names a source nobody pulled yet.
5. Send each chosen reply with the place's send tool (tool:send-a-reply-on-instagram or tool:send-a-reply-on-youtube), passing its decision.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and its fields. The tool matches each kit field to one of yours (by the map you give, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), refuses when fewer than least_coverage of the kit's fields match, and otherwise answers the records:write that adds the example rows to your list, leaving your own rows untouched.
